note: Obsidian facts for probes of its own syntax, per rule area. Lines only, 0-based: strict promises no columns. Sections drop element/text, the rendered footnote list no tree holds.

cases.name: F4 tab under quote then label
A4 def then ref on title line
indented closer
cases.excluded: Not a closer, so neither opens frontmatter; but under CommonMark ` ---` below a paragraph line is a setext underline, so strict reads `a: 1` as a heading. Obsidian's parser takes no indented underline, which is legacy's.

cases.name: old closer case
cases.excluded: An undefined `[^…` label is text under strict, as in GFM, so the `[[…]]` inside it is a wikilink and the `#` after it starts a tag. Obsidian's parser reads every `[^…]` as a reference first, before the wikilink can form.

cases.name: quoted tab second
cases.excluded: A tab after `>`: Obsidian defines nothing here, by its parser's tab arithmetic, which is legacy's. Strict reads the tab as CommonMark does, and the box and label as everywhere else.

cases.name: quoted tab first
cases.excluded: A tab after `>`: Obsidian defines nothing here, by its parser's tab arithmetic, which is legacy's. Strict reads the tab as CommonMark does, and the box and label as everywhere else.

cases.name: quote lazy bullet
cases.excluded: micromark ends a construct that runs to its container's end at column 1 of the next line when that line opens a list, so the quote's section reaches one line too far -- stock remark-parse does the same for a fenced code block in this shape. Obsidian syntax is read right: the bullet is not taken into the comment.

cases.name: quote lazy ordered 1
cases.excluded: micromark ends a construct that runs to its container's end at column 1 of the next line when that line opens a list, so the quote's section reaches one line too far -- stock remark-parse does the same for a fenced code block in this shape. Obsidian syntax is read right: the bullet is not taken into the comment.

cases.name: math tab quote label
cases.excluded: A tab after each `>`: Obsidian's tab arithmetic makes no math block of `$$` here, so the label below defines; strict reads the tabs as CommonMark does, and the math block keeps its lazy line as everywhere else.
